title: Grateful Dead Live at Buffalo Memorial Auditorium on 1973-03-31
lineage: Master Soundboard Reel > Cassette > DAT > CD-R

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1973 show highlighted by a smoking He's Gone > Truckin' > The Other One jam, stellar Playin', and a fiery Tennessee Jed solo.
ai_review.review: This recording delivers crisp, well‑balanced soundboard audio that lets the band’s tight, high‑octane performance shine. The second set rolls through an epic sequence – He's Gone into Truckin' then The Other One, followed by Spanish Jam and Playin' – with Jerry’s tone and solos in top form and Phil “bombing” on bass. Aside from occasional tuning pauses, the show is consistently exciting and musically rewarding.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews are 4‑5 stars praising both performance and sound; weighted average leans strongly toward a high‑quality show with excellent recording.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with good instrument separation; a few reviewers note slight hiss and occasional tuning pauses but overall the board sound is very listenable.

standout_songs: He's Gone > Truckin' > The Other One
show_quality.setlist_flow: A seamless flow of extended jams, especially in the second set where one long suite links He's Gone through Truckin', The Other One and Spanish Jam, creating a powerful momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Tone praised as “on” throughout; his solo on Tennessee Jed described as ferocious and the most exciting of his career era.
band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly called a ‘bomb’ – driving the jams, especially during Spanish Jam and the extended The Other One sequence.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for a right‑channel WDD figure tease and solid rhythm guitar throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith briefly joins on keyboards for a short segment; otherwise no specific keyboard commentary.
